design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial where a research consultant prepared the randomization code and consecutively numbered packages.

domain_judgments.rationale: The randomization code and sequentially numbered identical packages were prepared by an independent research consultant and distributed by a blinded research assistant, ensuring concealed allocation, and baseline characteristics showed no major imbalances.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A research consultant prepared the randomization code and the packages of medication (18). The packages were identical in appearance except for the randomization numbers. A research assistant who was blinded to treatment assignments distributed the study medication.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and study staff were blinded using identical lozenges, blinding was formally tested and maintained, adherence was tracked, and no important deviations from the intended protocol occurred.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The placebo and zinc lozenges were identical in weight (4000 mg), appearance, flavor, and texture... A research assistant who was blinded to treatment assignments distributed the study medication... Participants returned to the clinic for the final visit within 1 day of resolution of cold symptoms. At this time, they returned unused lozenges. This was done to check adherence and confirm that cold symptoms had resolved.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data were available for 48 out of 50 participants (96%), the dropout rate was very low (4%) with clear reasons provided, and the loss is unlikely to bias the results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two participants in the placebo group dropped out on day 2. We therefore had complete data on 48 participants... Twenty-five volunteers were initially recruited in each group. Two persons in the placebo group dropped out on day 2 and were lost to follow-up. One of the two persons had a sore mouth, and the other developed an ear infection for which care was transferred to a physician outside of Detroit Medical Center.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of cold symptom duration and severity was recorded by participants who were adequately blinded to their treatment assignment using identical placebo lozenges, and blinding assessment confirmed success.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were asked to complete a daily log documenting the severity of symptoms and the medications taken throughout the duration of the cold. Every day, the participants graded each symptom as 0 for none, 1 for mild, 2 for moderate, and 3 for severe... Resolution of cold symptoms was defined as resolution of all symptoms (a total symptom score of 0) or resolution of all but one mild symptom (a total symptom score of 1)... In addition, at the beginning of the trial, 48% of zinc recipients and 26% of placebo recipients correctly identified the lozenges (P > 0.2). At the end of the study, 56% of zinc recipients and 26% of placebo recipients correctly identified the lozenges (P = 0.09).

domain_judgments.rationale: The prespecified primary and secondary endpoints are clearly defined in the methods section and fully reported according to a standard statistical analysis plan without evidence of selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Our primary end point was the average duration of cold symptoms. Secondary end points were plasma levels of zinc and proinflammatory cytokines.

overall_summary: The study is a well-designed, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with central allocation concealment, documented blinding maintenance, minimal attrition (4%), and consistent reporting of prespecified outcomes, leading to a low risk of bias across all RoB 2 domains.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to zinc acetate or placebo lozenge groups using a pre-prepared randomization code.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was concealed using consecutively numbered, identical packages prepared by an independent research consultant, and baseline characteristics were comparable.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A research consultant prepared the randomization code and the packages of medication [21]. The packages were identical in appearance except for the randomization numbers. A research assistant who was blinded to treatment assignments distributed the study medication.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blinding was effectively maintained as confirmed by blinding assessments, and all 50 participants adhered to treatment and were analyzed in their assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The placebo and zinc lozenges were identical in weight, appearance, flavor, and texture and were supplied by George Eby. ... Participants were informed of the placebo-controlled, double-blind nature of the study ... The participants filled out a questionnaire in which they were asked to guess whether they had received zinc or placebo lozenges. ... Contingency analysis of correctness by group at the beginning of the study yielded P = 1.0 ... At the end of the study, the same test yielded P = .489.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for the primary outcome (duration of symptoms) and severity scores were complete for all 50 randomized participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Table 2 shows the duration and severity of cold symptoms in the zinc and placebo groups. ... Zinc group (n = 25) Placebo group (n = 25)

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome assessment was standardized and participants remained successfully blinded throughout the trial, minimizing measurement bias for self-reported symptoms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were asked to complete a daily log documenting the severity of symptoms and the medications taken throughout the duration of the cold. Every day the subjects graded each symptom as 0 for none, 1 for mild, 2 for moderate, or 3 for severe. Total symptom scores were calculated by summing the scores of the 10 symptoms for each day. Resolution of cold symptoms was defined as resolution of all symptoms (a total symptom score of 0) or resolution of all but 1 mild symptom (a total symptom score of 1). The participants were not asked to rate their overall illness or level of severity in order to make their assessments unbiased.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a prospective trial registration or published pre-specified statistical analysis plan, though the reported primary and secondary outcomes match those defined in the methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Our primary end point was the average duration of cold symptoms. Secondary end points were plasma levels of (1) zinc; (2) soluble interleukin (IL)-1 receptor antagonist (sIL-1ra) and soluble tumor necrosis factor (TNF) receptor (sTNF-R) 1; and (3) the plasma adhesion molecules, soluble vascular endothelial cell adhesion molecule (sVCAM)-1 and soluble ICAM (sICAM)-1.

overall_summary: The study is well-conducted and well-blinded with complete follow-up, but some concerns remain due to the lack of a prospective trial registration or published pre-specified statistical analysis plan.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial in which a pharmacist used a randomization table provided by the study statistician to assign 87 participants to treatment groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: An adequate random allocation sequence was generated by a statistician, allocation was concealed via a third-party pharmacist pre-packaging identical containers, and baseline characteristics between groups were balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization by a third party was used to assign the 87 participants to treatment groups. A pharmacist, using a randomization table provided by the study statistician, packaged containers for individual subjects with lozenges according to the production run number and subject identification number. Patients, investigators and the pharmacist were, therefore, all blinded as to which treatment individual patients had received.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and trial personnel were effectively blinded using a taste- and appearance-matched placebo (confirmed by blinding assessment), and no major protocol deviations were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients, investigators and the pharmacist were, therefore, all blinded as to which treatment individual patients had received... At their final visits, the patients were asked by the nurse which treatment they thought they had received... The resulting χ2-value of 0.8975 was not significant; thus, the patients did not know which treatment they had received.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was low (16% overall: 8/43 in ZGG, 6/44 in placebo), balanced across groups, with reasons documented and unlikely to be related to the true outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of eight ZGG- and six placebo-treated patients withdrew from the trial leaving 35 and 38 evaluable patients, respectively. Illnesses that resulted in patients withdrawing from the study were as follows: two patients had bronchitis and one had viral gastro-enteritis in the placebo treatment group; and there was one patient with influenza and one with a bacterial infection in the ZGG treatment group. Other reasons for withdrawing were: failure to appear at follow-up (three ZGG- and one placebo-treated patient); efficacy doubted by the patient (one ZGG- and one placebo-treated patient); nausea (one ZGG- and one placebo-treated patient); and sports injury (one ZGG-treated patient).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were self-reported cold symptoms recorded in standardized diaries, and successful double-blinding minimized the risk of detection bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients kept diaries recording the severity of their symptoms upon enrollment, at 6 and 12 h after the first dose of the study medication, and at 20.00 h on each subsequent day. They were instructed to rate the severity of 10 cold symptoms on a scale of 0 – 3 (0, none; 1, mild; 2, moderate; and 3, severe)...

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a priori planning for subgroup analysis is mentioned, no trial registration or pre-published protocol was available, which leaves some concern for selective reporting among multiple symptom metrics and time points.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the present study, the strict criterion of complete disappearance of all symptoms was used as the definition of the cold being over... It was planned a priori to test the effect of day of entry on duration of the cold after entering study.

overall_summary: The trial was well conducted with centralized randomization, effective blinding, and low attrition, but lack of a pre-registered protocol gives some concerns regarding selection of reported results across multiple symptom definitions and time points.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in which 213 participants were randomly assigned to receive zinc nasal gel (n = 108) or placebo (n = 105).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the authors state participants were randomly assigned, no information is provided regarding sequence generation, allocation concealment, or baseline characteristics of the two groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study population consisted of 213 subjects; they were randomly assigned to receive either zinc nasal gel (n = 108) or placebo (n = 105).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind using an identical placebo gel and matched metered-dose applicators, with no reported deviations from protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The zinc nasal gel consisted of zinc gluconate in an emulsion of benzalkonium chloride, glycerin, hydroxyethylcellulose, sodium chloride, and sodium hydroxide; its pH level was 7.2. The composition of the placebo gel was identical except that it did not contain zinc. Both gels were dispensed in a double-blind fashion in metered doses of 120 µl in applicators supplied by Botanical Laboratories (Ferndale, Wash.).

domain_judgments.rationale: All 213 enrolled participants appear to be accounted for in the results (108 zinc, 105 placebo), with no reported dropouts or missing diary data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study group consisted of 213 patients with recent-onset (≤24 hr) cold symptoms; 108 patients received zinc therapy, and 105 received placebo... At study's end, the duration of symptoms was 2.3 days (±0.9) in the zinc group and 9.0 days (±2.5) in the control group

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome measurement relied on patient diaries and clinician verification under double-blind conditions with identical applicators and placebo, making assessment bias unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were provided with a diary to document the severity of their symptoms... The primary endpoint was the complete resolution of symptoms, which was determined when the total symptom score fell to zero. Subjects were asked to return to their study site within 24 hours of symptom resolution for verification and followup.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial protocol or registration is cited, leaving some concern regarding potential selective reporting of predefined outcomes or analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was the complete resolution of symptoms, which was determined when the total symptom score fell to zero.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to the lack of reporting on sequence generation, allocation concealment, baseline comparability, and pre-specified trial protocol/registration.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either zinc gluconate glycine lozenges or placebo using a computer-generated randomization code held by the pharmacist.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated by computer and concealed by the pharmacist who held the code and prepared identical packages, resulting in comparable baseline groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A computer-generated randomization code was provided to the pharmacist, who held the code and prepared the packages of medication. The packages were identical in appearance, except for the identifying code number, and were distributed to the study personnel, all of whom were masked to the group assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was double-blinded, adherence was tracked and balanced across groups, deviations were minimal, and an intention-to-treat analysis approach was implemented for the primary outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two students, who were determined to be ineligible after assignment, were included in these analyses, in keeping with the intent-to-treat principle, and were treated as censored observations with a cold duration of 0.001 days.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 249 randomized students were included in the primary time-to-event analysis using standard survival analysis methods for censored observations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Ten students' (3 placebo, 7 active) colds did not resolve during the period of observation. Thus, statistical methods for incomplete data were used. Resolution rates were calculated using the method of Kaplan and Meier, and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the estimates of median time to resolution were calculated using the method of Brookmeyer and Crowley.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was participant-reported subjective symptom duration, and zinc lozenges caused distinct adverse effects (bad taste, throat irritation) that led to significant unblinding among participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Students were asked to indicate whether they thought they were taking the active drug, the placebo, or whether they didn't know on day 2 and at the conclusion of the study... A significantly higher proportion of students receiving zinc (46% [55/119]) guessed correctly than did controls (24% [30/123]); P = .001) on day 2... The students who received zinc experienced significantly more bad taste reactions; nausea; mouth, tongue, or throat irritation; and diarrhea than those in the placebo group

domain_judgments.rationale: The study reported outcomes in line with predefined primary and secondary objectives and standard analytical approaches for time-to-event cold resolution data without signs of selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary analyses of resolution time were performed using Cox proportional hazards regression models and the method devised by Efron to adjust for the large number of patients with identical resolution times.

overall_summary: The study was generally well-conducted with computer-generated central allocation concealment and intention-to-treat analysis, but some concerns exist regarding outcome measurement due to subjective participant-reported cold symptom scoring combined with imperfect masking evidenced by significantly higher rates of adverse taste/irritation effects and correct treatment guesses in the zinc group.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned using a computer-generated randomization code in blocks of 10 prepared by an independent company.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed until assignment by an independent third party, and baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An independent company, Botanicals International, prepared a computer-generated randomization code for the hand-held nasal pumps that remained concealed until the treatment assignment. This company was the only party that knew of the actual treatment assignment before enrolment. Randomization was performed in blocks of 10 (5 zinc and 5 placebo).

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and trial personnel were effectively blinded using identical sprays, blinding was evaluated on day 1 with no significant unmasking, and an intention-to-treat analysis included all patients except two lost to follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To ensure blinding of patients to treatment assignment, all pumps were identical in appearance except for the randomization numbers. The physician who examined the patients at enrolment and the clinical research coordinator that distributed the pumps were blinded to the treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 2 out of 80 participants (2.5%) were lost to follow-up, which is a very low attrition rate unlikely to introduce substantial bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An intention-to-treat analysis of the primary outcome measure, the time to cold resolution, was performed for all enrolled patients, except two from the placebo group who were lost to follow-up and did not return their symptoms scores charts.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although outcomes were self-reported symptoms, participants and investigators were blinded to treatment allocation, minimizing the risk of biased measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The investigator who assessed the outcomes was blinded to the treatment assignment until all patients were enrolled and returned their symptoms score charts.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan, though outcomes reported align with standard methods in the field.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measure was the time to cold resolution, calculated as the number of days starting from the onset of symptoms till their complete resolution. The secondary outcome measures were the total daily symptom scores and the presence of adverse effects.

overall_summary: The trial was well conducted with sound randomization, allocation concealment, double-blinding, and minimal attrition, but lack of evidence of an independent pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified analysis plan raises some concerns for selection of the reported result.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to receive either 0.12% zinc sulfate or placebo nasal spray using block randomization prepared by the manufacturer.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated in blocks of four, central pre-packaging/coding concealed allocation, and baseline characteristics were comparable between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The active and placebo nasal spray bottles were randomly placed in blocks of four by the manufacturer (CNS Inc., Minneapolis, Minnesota). The spray dispensers were identical in appearance except for an identifying code number. All study personnel were blinded to the group assignments. The manufacturer held the randomization key until all participants had completed the protocol and the data were entered.

domain_judgments.rationale: Post-randomization exclusions occurred based on post-baseline events (antibiotic use during study, early discontinuation) and a modified ITT/per-protocol approach rather than full intention-to-treat analysis was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Twenty-five (14%) patients were excluded because of laboratory-confirmed influenza (n = 8), antibiotic therapy for bacterial infection (n = 7), symptoms for longer than 24 hours (n = 6), concurrent use of zinc lozenges (n = 2), or history of allergic rhinitis (n = 1). One patient was excluded because the nasal spray was discontinued on the day of enrollment, and the exit interview was not completed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for virtually all 160 analyzed participants, with sensitivity analysis using imputation yielding consistent results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For determining resolution, missing symptoms were assumed to be zero for the primary analysis, but the analyses were repeated after imputing missing values based on the previous and subsequent days... When the analysis was repeated with imputation of missing symptom scores, the result was unchanged (P = 0.43).

domain_judgments.rationale: Symptom reporting was participant-assessed, but successful double-blinding (tested at exit interview with no differential guessing) minimized risk of bias in outcome measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Each patient completed a diary card twice a day to record oral temperature, symptoms, and adverse effects... During the exit interview, 22 (27%) participants in the zinc group and 18 (23%) in the placebo group guessed that they received the zinc preparation (P = 0.59).

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registered protocol was cited, and post-hoc analyses adjusting for baseline covariates were conducted across multiple days and symptom subgroups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In a posthoc analysis, total symptom scores were further analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) to adjust for the observed differences in symptom severity at baseline.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to post-randomization exclusions of participants based on events occurring during the study period and the use of post-hoc baseline-adjusted analyses without an available pre-specified statistical analysis protocol.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled clinical trial investigating zinc acetate lozenges versus placebo for common cold symptoms.

domain_judgments.rationale: The article states that the study was randomized, but no details are provided regarding the method of sequence generation or allocation concealment. Baseline characteristics appear balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because this was a randomized, double-masked study, subjects were informed that some individuals would receive zinc lozenges and some would receive placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-masking was implemented using matched placebo lozenges with taste-masking, and there is no evidence of deviations from the intended protocol or failure of blinding that affected the intervention delivery.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To achieve masking, sucrose octaacetate (0.169 mg) was used in the placebo, and both the placebo and zinc lozenges were peppermint flavored.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 101 of 102 randomized participants (99%), with only one subject lost to follow-up, making bias due to missing data negligible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patient diaries were completed by 101 subjects; 1 subject was lost to follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessment was self-reported symptom duration and severity using daily diaries, and participants were successfully blinded to assignment with an active placebo designed to match taste.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Subjects were also informed that they were required to rate and record their symptoms in a diary at the same time each day.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no evidence of a prospective clinical trial registry or pre-published statistical analysis plan, and multiple outcome definitions for symptom duration and individual symptoms were tested.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Table II shows the mean duration of all symptoms (duration of each symptom ÷ number of symptoms), the mean duration of the longest-lasting symptom (symptom with the longest duration), and the mean severity rating (a mean score for all symptoms) by treatment group.

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to lack of reported details regarding random sequence generation and allocation concealment, as well as the absence of a prospective trial registration or pre-specified analysis plan.
